$comment: Stage 9 manifest.json, byte-exact in shape. Field names are the whole interop: serde and JSONEncoder default to different styles, so both platforms write what THIS file says and both read it back. The example is deliberately a partial download — `pagesCount` is the book's total and `pages` lists only what is on disk, page 5 missing — because that is the state a manifest is written in most often and the one an implementation could get wrong by assuming the two are equal. It is also the state that makes 边下边读 work: a reader asks for page 3, finds it here, and never learns page 5 is not.

fieldRules.serverId_bookId: Raw ids as the server knows them, NOT the sanitised directory names. A `safe_key` collision between two servers would otherwise be invisible: the manifest is the only document that can say which book this really is.
fieldRules.downloadedAt: When this book's download was created, RFC 3339 in UTC with second precision and a `Z` suffix. Rewritten only when the job is created, never when a page lands — a download of a 292-page book has one creation time, and 292 different page times would make the field unusable for the freshness comparison.
fieldRules.remoteLastModified: The book's `lastModified` as the server reported it when the job was created. Compared against `books.last_modified` after a sync, it is what lets the UI say 内容已更新 instead of silently serving a stale copy. `null` when the job was created offline and never saw a server answer.
fieldRules.pages: Ascending by `number`, completed pages only. `fileName` is relative to the directory holding this manifest, never absolute, so a user moving the app's storage container keeps a readable library.
fieldRules.sizeBytes: The size the file actually ended up being, read back from the filesystem after the rename — not what the server declared. A declared size is a claim; this one is a measurement.
fieldRules.width_height: 0 when unknown. The manifest mirror already carries the server's values and a download must not invent dimensions it was never told.

rewrittenOn: enqueue (the empty-pages form, which is what makes a directory self-describing before any byte arrives)
any user delete of a page within the book
notWrittenPerPage: A pass commits its row per page anyway, so a per-page manifest rewrite is O(n) extra writes for zero extra durability, and the directory listing already proves what is present. This will look like a bug to whoever reads it next; it is not one.
